e1.location: nist_asd_2026/level_Xe_odd_J1: row 1, 5p5.(2P*<3/2>).6s 2[3/2]* J = 1, the level energy
e1.derivation: the level energy in cm^-1, times 100

uncertainty.provenance: nist_asd_2026/level_Xe_odd_J1: the source states none (its printed precision is not one)

qualifications: The lowest odd-parity J = 1 level, 5p5 6s [3/2]1: the lowest dipole-coupled to the 5p6 1S0 ground level.

e2.location: nist_asd_2026/level_Xe_even_J2: row 1, 5p5.(2P*<3/2>).6p 2[5/2] J = 2, the level energy
e2.derivation: the smallest of the candidates; the level energy in cm^-1, times 100

uncertainty.provenance: nist_asd_2026/level_Xe_even_J2: the source states none (its printed precision is not one)

qualifications: The lowest even-parity levels of J = 0 and 2 (5p5 6p), reached by two photons through the symmetric part of the two-photon tensor. An even J = 1 level is reached only through its antisymmetric part, which vanishes for one common linear polarisation (DeMille et al. 1999, eqs. 1-4).
Lehmberg et al.'s two-photon resonance with 6p[1/2]0, at a 249.6 nm fundamental, lies above this level (TC-854).

e2_any.derivation: the smallest of the candidates; the level energy in cm^-1, times 100

uncertainty.provenance: nist_asd_2026/level_Xe_even_J1: the source states none (its printed precision is not one)

qualifications: The smallest of the lowest even-parity levels of J = 0, 1 and 2: for any polarisation the antisymmetric part of the two-photon tensor reaches J = 1. It vanishes for two photons of equal frequency.
